items.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015
items.q: Woody would not be around. We would work things up without him around and then he would ask me if it was good enough to call on the gig.

ctx.x: And do you like it that way?

I do, I do. When I first moved to New York I did anything and everything, as one would want to do when you move to a new city, including Broadway and commercial work, and a lot of I guess you could say non-creative type of things, where they just need someone to come in and play trombone or someone to write a certain number of measures or whatever. But through my past experiences touring with Woody Herman and other people, I just really worked toward that my entire life. And after getting off the road, to me it…
By banging it out do you mean like getting a pit band job for “The Lion King” and just doing that until —
